For the purposes of this article, domestic violence means (( one or more acts, serious or non-episodic, )) of physical, sexual, psychological or economic violence occurring within the family or family unit (( or between persons linked, currently or in the past, by a marriage bond or by an emotional relationship, )) regardless of whether the perpetrator of such acts shares or has shared the same residence with the victim.
When, in the course of police operations, investigations or proceedings for any of the offenses provided for in articles 572, 582, 583, 583-bis, 605, 609-bis and 612-bis of the criminal code or for one of the offenses provided for in article 380 of the code of criminal procedure, committed on the national territory in the context of domestic violence, situations of violence or abuse against a foreigner are ascertained and a concrete and current danger to his or her safety emerges, as a consequence of the choice to escape from the same violence or as a result of the statements made during the preliminary investigations or the trial, the questore, (( with the favorable opinion of the proceeding judicial authority or upon proposal of the latter, )) issues a residence permit pursuant to article 5, paragraph 6, to allow the victim to escape from the violence.

6.1.rationale: The policy establishes civil society participation in VAW policy design and implementation: the Minister prepares the national action plan with the contribution of women’s associations and anti-violence centres, and it explicitly provides that anti-violence centres and shelters are promoted by associations/organizations supporting women victims of violence (including in joint arrangements). These are operative provisions creating formal roles for NGOs/CSOs in VAW prevention/response.

6.2.rationale: Across the provided sentences, the framework references women’s associations, anti-violence centres, schools, media operators, and institutions generally, but it does not mention religious organisations/leaders or traditional/cultural organisations/leaders as partners or participants in VAW prevention or response.

6.3.rationale: The action plan includes operative purposes that involve schools directly, including training school staff and integrating awareness-raising, information, and training of students within curricular and extra-curricular educational programming across school levels to prevent violence against women and gender discrimination. This constitutes engagement with education institutions for VAW prevention.

6.4.rationale: The only international reference in the candidate sentences is that the plan must be prepared “in synergy with the new programming of the European Union for the period 2014-2020,” which does not clearly establish or require cooperation with an international organisation on VAW (it reads as alignment with EU programming rather than an operative collaboration mechanism with an international organisation). No other operative provisions identify international organisations as partners for VAW prevention/response.

6.5.rationale: The plan’s purposes explicitly include raising awareness among media sector operators and promoting respectful communication/information (including via self-regulatory codes). This is an operative provision that engages media actors in VAW-related prevention and norm change.

6.6.rationale: While the plan includes community awareness-raising as an objective, the provided sentences do not establish a mechanism for community participation/collaboration (e.g., community organisations or public members as partners) in VAW prevention/response; it frames the community as the target of information/awareness rather than as an engaged actor. The other provisions concern institutions and service networks rather than community participation mechanisms.

6.7.indicator: Engagement/collaboration with business and private sector
6.7.rationale: The candidate sentences do not establish or require collaboration with businesses or private-sector actors for VAW prevention or response. References to “media sector operators” relate to media engagement (not general private sector), and mentions of “public and private” anti-violence centres/shelters describe service availability rather than private-sector partnership obligations or mechanisms.
